To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the Na+/K+ pump of the cardiac sarcolemma is activated by adrenaline, and this activation results in a higher rate of Na+ transport without increasing the coupling ratio or the number of pumping sites.
adrenaline increases electrogenic Na+ extrusion from cardiac cells without increasing the Na+/K+ coupling ratio.
adrenaline enhances the electrogenic sodium pump current in cardiac muscle cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of adrenaline on cardiac muscle fibres of bullfrog atria and on isolated ventricular myocytes of rat heart.
the study of the electrogenic Na+-pump in cardiac muscle cells and its interaction with the Na+-channel and the Na+-K+ pump.
the effect of adrenaline on cardiac Na+ pump activity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the effect of adrenaline on Na+ pump currents in frog atrium is due to an increase in the rate of the Na+/K+ exchange.
adrenaline increases the Na+ pump current by increasing the turnover rate of the Na+ pump.
adrenaline increases the electrogenic Na pump current by increasing the number of open Na pump sites, without changing the coupling ratio.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
adrenaline increases the Na/K pump rate in the heart without changing its stoichiometry.
adrenaline activates the Na+ pump by increasing the rate of Na+/K+ exchange at each pumping site.
the electrogenic Na-pump current is increased by adrenaline.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we can now study the effects of drugs on the cardiac Na/K pump in a living animal model.
the electrogenic sodium pump is a potential therapeutic target for treating heart failure.
the electrogenic Na pump can contribute to the action potential in cardiac muscle.
